headline: ACTIVIST ELLIOTT TAKES $1B STAKE in Northern Star, Demands Australia's Top Gold Miner Weigh Sale
snippet: Elliott Investment Management built a stake of more than A$1 billion in Northern Star Resources (ASX: NST) and called for a full strategic review, including a possible sale. NST shares surged 14% to A$21.03 — the stock's biggest single-day gain in six years. Analysts say the move could trigger a broader wave of M&A activity across the gold sector.

headline: CENTRAL ASIA METALS BIDS A$232M for TSXV Copper Junior Cygnus at 60% Premium
snippet: Central Asia Metals (AIM: CAML) proposed an all-share acquisition of Cygnus Metals (TSXV: CYG, ASX: CY5) for approximately A$232 million — a 60% premium to Cygnus' last closing price. The deal targets Cygnus' Chibougamau copper project in Québec, with shareholders voting expected in September.

headline: URENCO TO ADD 50% MORE U.S. URANIUM ENRICHMENT Capacity With Multibillion New Mexico Plant
snippet: Urenco USA announced a multibillion-dollar expansion of its National Enrichment Facility in Eunice, New Mexico, adding 2.1 million separative work units of new low enriched uranium capacity. Construction begins 2029, with first production targeted for 2032 — a significant long-term demand signal for Western uranium miners.

headline: DOE AWARDS $134M to Pull Rare Earths From Industrial Waste — No New Mines Required
snippet: The U.S. Department of Energy awarded $134 million across two projects to extract and refine rare earth elements from mine tailings and alumina refinery 'red mud.' The Colorado School of Mines / ElementUSA project in Louisiana targets 150–1,000 tonnes of REEs annually from 30 million tonnes of existing industrial waste.

headline: GOLD BOUNCES TO $4,523 After Monday Slide as Silver Jumps 1.9% to $76.67
snippet: Gold spot recovered to $4,523/oz (+0.70%) as a pullback in oil prices tempered inflation fears, even as US-Iran peace talks stalled. Silver climbed to $76.67/oz (+1.87%), with technical support at $75.31 holding firm. The Fed's June 17 meeting is now the key near-term catalyst for precious metals direction.

headline: TRUMP SIGNS NEW METALS TARIFF PROCLAMATION Widening U.S. Copper Premium, Effective June 8
snippet: President Trump signed a June 1 proclamation further adjusting Section 232 tariffs on copper, steel, and aluminum, effective June 8 through December 2027. The update has widened the US copper premium and is spurring investment in domestic copper mining and smelting capacity from firms including Rio Tinto and Ivanhoe Electric.

headline: COPPER ABOVE $6.50/LB Near Two-Week Highs as Chile Q1 Output Falls 5.8%
snippet: Copper futures climbed above $6.50/lb, supported by tightening global supply and robust demand from the AI data centre buildout. Chile's Q1 output fell 5.8% year-on-year, compounding concerns after Codelco's internal audit revealed the state miner's actual 2025 production sank to a 27-year low.

headline: GLENCORE DECLARES FORCE MAJEURE at Cerrejón as Community Blockade Halts Colombian Coal Mine
snippet: Glencore declared force majeure at its Cerrejón coal mine on June 1 after community protesters blocked the railway to Puerto Bolívar, halting coal shipments and cutting off fuel delivery. The blockade — timed to Colombia's upcoming presidential runoff — follows community demands for ancestral land repatriation and environmental reparations.

headline: SINGAPORE FIRM BOROO EYES EAGLE GOLD MINE But Yukon Community Raises Rehabilitation Questions
snippet: Singapore-based Boroo Pte. Ltd. entered exclusive talks with receiver PwC to acquire Victoria Gold's former Eagle Gold mine near Mayo, Yukon — site of a catastrophic 2024 cyanide tailings spill. Industry observers are questioning whether the little-known firm has the financial depth and technical expertise to manage a complex remediation.

headline: SECOND CHINA MINE DISASTER in 10 Days Kills 5 in Yunnan, Beijing Launches National Safety Sweep
snippet: An illegal gold mine in Yunnan province collapsed May 31, killing 5 workers, days after China's Shanxi coal blast killed 82 — the country's deadliest mining accident in 15 years. Beijing's ensuing safety crackdown is expected to force shutdowns at hundreds of smaller private mines, temporarily constraining domestic coal supply.

headline: GOLD-SILVER RATIO Compresses Near Multi-Year Low — Analysts See Silver Set to Outperform Gold
snippet: With gold near $4,500/oz and silver pushing toward $77/oz, the gold-to-silver ratio has compressed to levels historically associated with silver outperformance. Analysts highlight strong industrial and Chinese investment demand as key drivers, with silver now in its sixth consecutive year of structural market deficits.
